processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 39 kg low-density steel ingot with composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P produced via vacuum induction melting
The ingot was hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) × 70 mm (width) × 40 mm (thickness)
Billets heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min before hot rolling
High-rigidity two-roll mill; six passes with 90% cumulative reduction; began at 1100 °C, finish rolling at 880 °C; final thickness 4 mm; air cooled
Four-roll reversible mill, 60% reduction, resulting thickness 1.6 mm
Annealed within the critical region and air-cooled to room temperature; sample labeled AN750

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase microstructure with a strongly banded, wavy lath structure composed of ferrite, bainite, fresh martensite and retained austenite

phases_present.morphology: Carbon-depleted regions form ferrite; bainite distributes along ferrite grain boundaries
Distributes along ferrite grain boundaries, forming regions about 3 µm in size
Attached to the bainite; islands comprising fresh martensite and retained austenite
Sparse small FCC (RA) grains in a BCC matrix

interfaces.phase_evolution: During intercritical annealing, portions of bainite and martensite reaustenitize due to the high solubility of carbon in austenite, causing carbon enrichment and enhanced austenite stability; carbon-depleted regions form ferrite, some carbon-enriched austenite is retained during cooling as retained austenite, unstabilized austenite undergoes diffusionless transformation during cooling to form fresh martensite, and bainite forms during cooling in regions not fully austenitized

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Field emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FEI Quanta-650 FEG)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etched with 4% nitric acid ethanol solution; electropolished using 80% ethanol, 15% perchloric acid, 5% glycerol at 28 V and 0.1 A for 15–30 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the multiphase microstructure of AN750
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750 retains a strongly banded, wavy lath structure with bainite and fresh martensite; bainite forms regions about 3 µm along ferrite grain boundaries with attached fresh martensite or FM+RA islands

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 kV operating voltage; scanning step size 0.2 µm; TSL OIM 7.0; BCC and FCC phases indexed; minimum pixel size 9
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution, retained austenite content and RA grain size in AN750
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750 phase fractions FCC 0.030 / BCC 0.970; retained austenite content 3.0 vol%; RA average grain size D_AVE = 0.59 µm

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Rolling plane; accelerating voltage 40 kV; tube current 40 mA; scanning angle range 30°–110°
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases and confirm retained austenite in AN750
characterization_methods.key_findings: γ (FCC) reflections confirm retained austenite present in AN750

unmapped_findings: The mechanical tensile values reported in the paper (yield strength 697 MPa, tensile strength 1068 MPa, elongation 34.0%, PSE 36.3 GPa%) correspond to AN750-T (750 °C annealing plus 400 °C/30 min low-bainite aging), not to the AN750 sample defined here (750 °C/30 min intercritical annealing, air-cooled, no aging). No tensile, hardness, or other mechanical property values are reported for the non-aged AN750 sample itself.
